newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria president calls for massive vote on June 5.
newsitem.headline: Algeria president calls for massive vote on June 5.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual told his 29 million people on Friday that parliamentary elections would be held on June 5 to end instability that had undermined the country.

Algeria has been without a parliament since January 1992 when army-backed authorities cancelled a poll in which the radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead. Violence erupted shortly afterwards and an estimated 60,000 people have since died.

"From now on, for the third time, you are invited to the ballot box to express your viewpoint in the national process to put an end to institutional instability which undermined our country," he said.
The date of June 5 had already been announced by state-run radio last Tuesday, quoting a presidential statement, but under the constitution the president had to tell the people in a national address.
Algerian held its first multi-candidate presidential election in 1995 and Zeroual was confirmed in the post to which he had earlier been appointed without ballot.
The presidential poll was followed by a referendum last year to change the constitution.

In his 20-minute speech on Algerian television, Zeroual added: "This is an opportunity for you to express your choice freely and in transparency. I pledge in the name of the state, before God, and before you to respect the choice that you express."
He called on civil servants to mobilise to ensure the success of this "historic event" for the North African country's democracy and multi-party system.
A special commission to supervise the elections, and the invitation to international observers to monitor the poll, "aimed to guarantee the credibility of the polls", he said.
The outlawed FIS is barred from taking part in the poll which will introduce proportional representation in place of the majority, first-past-the-post method previously used.
Algerian authorities see the election as a way of ending the violence which has shaken the country.

"By your massive participation at the ballot and by your sovereign choice, you will not only accomplish a national duty but you will by the same step re-establish confidence and concretise hope for Algeria," Zeroual said.
"The last word now returns to you."
